summary: Weekly co-sell pipeline review with Aurora Partners. Reviewed three priority joint deals (NovaHealth, Meridian Systems, and Zephyr Retail), discussed technical readiness, next steps for benchmarking and executive intro cadence, and clarified responsibilities for close plan and pricing. Identified security/compliance questions for NovaHealth and a potential objection around latency/cost tradeoffs. Agreed to run a Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted benchmark and update the joint deck.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Verma (Redwood SE), Samira Khan (Aurora Channel Lead), Liam O'Connor (Aurora Sales Director), Nina Alvarez (Aurora Solution Architect)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, do you see my screen?
[00:10] Samira: yep, can see it, thanks jordan.
[00:28] Jordan: cool so quick agenda, pipeline review, who we should be targeting for exec intros, any blockers on the technical side, and then pricing cadence. priya will jump in on benchmarks.
[00:42] Priya: hi all, i'll go through the tech frame and the recommended benchmark for novahealth.
[00:55] Liam: great, we've got 3 deals to run through - novahealth (healthcare payer), meridian systems (finserv analytics), zephyr retail (omnichannel). main thing from our side is timing: q2 target for novahealth, q3 for meridian.
[01:20] Jordan: ok novahealth is top priority, samira mentioned the buyer is the clinical ops lead, correct?
[01:28] Samira: yes that's right, sara kim, she cares a lot about PHI handling and auditability.
[01:35] Priya: perfect, so from redwood side we should highlight our private deployment option and KMS integrations. i'll propose a dedicated run first to prove latency and token cost, and then we can show hosted as fallback. note: private was miss-spelled on the doc once as 'prviate', so ignore that.
[01:58] Nina: couple clarifying q's - does redwood provide SOC2 type 2 attestation and per-request audit logs? novahealth will ask.
[02:10] Jordan: yes we have SOC 2 and iso in place, and the console has request-level tracing. i'll pull the security pack after this meeting.
[02:25] Samira: excellent. what about data residency - can we keep models & logs in us-east only?
[02:33] Priya: yes, we can pin region, we also have on-prem options. for the benchmark i'd like to run two configs: dedicated gpus in us-east and hosted with kv-cache on - to compare latency/cost.
[02:52] Liam: perfect. timing wise we need an exec intro week of feb 27th to keep q2 motion. can aurora intro to sara that week?
[03:02] Samira: yes i'll intro on feb 26/27.

[03:15] Jordan: quick pass on meridian systems - they care about throughput for batch scoring and cost per embedding. their legal is also pretty heavyweight.
[03:27] Nina: for meridian we'd likely recommend redwood dedicated with reserved capacity, and some quantization guidance. will priya be able to estimate token costs?
[03:36] Priya: i'll run a small cost model - i'll need sample payloads, about ~20k records. nina can you share a sample?
[03:44] Nina: yes i'll anonymize and send.
[03:48] Jordan: noted, action item: nina to send sample by next thursday.

[04:00] Priya: on zephyr retail - it's more POC-y, they want recommendations on reranking & structured outputs for search. lower compliance bar but latency is key in storefront. maybe hosted plus caching.
[04:15] Liam: zephyr wants a quick win for buy-shelf personalization, timeline is aggressive - demo by mid-march.

[04:30] Jordan: ok let's talk risks/objections - for novahealth i expect a security comittee review, possible resistance to hosted solutions. for meridian, cost per-embedding objection. for zephyr, we might see pushback on integration effort.
[04:48] Samira: right and aurora will push for joint pricing - we need a clear discount matrix and commit levels.
[04:56] Jordan: i'll update the co-sell deck and pricing sheet and share a link after the call. (link: https://redwood.share/cosell-deck-aurora). apologies if that link 404s right now, i'll confirm.

[05:10] Priya: technical detail - for novahealth benchmarks i suggest testing two sequence lengths: clinical note (avg 512 tokens) and short triage prompts (avg 128). we'll measure p50/p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens. also check kv-cache impact for repeated prefixes.
[05:32] Nina: sounds good, how long will a benchmark run take?
[05:36] Priya: depends, but initial pass maybe 48 hours to get stable numbers if we have the sample data ready. full load test might be a week.

[05:50] Jordan: ok next let's align owners - jordan to lead sales motion and pricing, priya to own benchmarks, samira to coordinate intros and field marketing support from aurora.
[06:02] Samira: yes and i'll make time to join the exec intro.

[06:10] Liam: one competitive note - novahealth mentioned they spoke with databricks and cohere around embeddings, we should be ready to show cost/perf delta and our private options.
[06:24] Priya: yeah i'll include a short perf slide and note differences in quantization and kernel support. sometimes our runtime names get garbled in decks, like 'Redwwod Optimize' or 'Redwood Dedciated' - so i'll make sure spelling is clean.

[06:40] Jordan: good catch. pricing - aurora, are you comfortable with a joint discounting approach tied to commit levels?
[06:48] Samira: yes but need clarity on contract owners. aurora prefers to be the reseller and handle first year invoicing. we will need a reseller agreement and SOW templates.
[06:58] Jordan: ok legal will loop in. i'll put together a reseller SOW draft and share.

[07:08] Nina: one more technical ask - novahealth will want model explainability logs for audit. does redwood capture per-inference logits or token probabilities in logs?
[07:20] Priya: we can capture scoring info in the audit logs but need to check retention policy. i'll confirm what fields are recorded and if we can include token-level scores for the audit.
[07:32] Jordan: action item for priya to confirm audit log fields and retention.

[07:45] Samira: for the intro to novahealth i can draft a battlecard for the execs. jordan, can you include a brief 1-pager on our co-sell value prop?
[07:54] Jordan: yes i'll do a 1-pager, keep it <1 page.

[08:02] (brief crosstalk)
[08:10] Priya: i'll schedule the benchmark kickoff once nina sends the data; planning to run dedicated vs hosted with kv-cache config.

[08:22] Jordan: timeline recap: intro feb 26/27, benchmark kickoff first week of march, pricing deck update by feb 23.

[08:30] Liam: sounds aligned. any blockers from aurora on the resell model?
[08:36] Samira: legal review timeline could be 2-3 weeks but shouldn't block q2 intro.

[08:45] Jordan: okay great. last thing - does anyone need a deeper technical workshop? we can run a 60 min deep dive for novahealth engineers next week.

[08:54] Nina: yes please, that would help. schedule it the week of march 2.

[09:02] Jordan: perfect, priya will run it.

[09:10] (wrap up)
[09:15] Jordan: recap of next steps: I'll send updated co-sell deck and joint pricing (by 2026-02-23), Priya will prepare benchmark plan and confirm audit log fields (kickoff first week of march), Samira will intro to Sara at NovaHealth (target 2026-02-26/27) and share Q1 campaign calendar. Nina to send anonymized sample data for meridian.
[09:42] Samira: got it, will action.
[09:45] Liam: thanks everyone.
[09:48] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and update the shared sheet. meeting adjourned.
